question.text: Another new investor subscribes to Kaveri Macro Fund during a DRAWDOWN — the NAV is Rs. 950, but HWM is Rs. 1,000 (the fund is Rs. 50 below HWM). Performance fee is 20%. Under the equalisation mechanism, what happens when the fund subsequently recovers from Rs. 950 back to Rs. 1,000 (a rise of Rs. 50)?

answer.text: The new investor pays 20% performance fee on the Rs. 50 recovery — i.e., Rs. 10 per unit — like existing investors
The new investor is exempt from performance fee until the NAV crosses Rs. 1,050

The new investor receives an equalisation DEBIT (contingent liability) equal to 20% x Rs. 50 = Rs. 10 per unit so that ON RECOVERY TO HWM, the new investor shares the performance-fee payment fairly with existing investors who already experienced the drawdown
The new investor is charged a 5% entry load

explanation.text: The Logic: When a new investor subscribes during a drawdown (NAV Rs. 950, HWM Rs. 1,000), without an adjustment the investor would benefit from the recovery from Rs. 950 to Rs. 1,000 free of performance fee — while existing investors, who experienced the drawdown, also pay nothing on that same recovery (their NAV is still below HWM). To keep cohorts fair, an equalisation DEBIT (contingent liability) of 20% x Rs. 50 = Rs. 10 per unit is booked against the new investor, so the recovery to the existing HWM is treated symmetrically across subscription dates. The Trap: Option A ignores the cohort-fairness mismatch the debit is designed to correct. Option B overstates the exemption — the new investor is not simply exempt until Rs. 1,050. Option D (entry load) is unrelated. Note: The equalisation-debit / contingent-liability accounting and drawdown-recovery mechanics described above are not explicitly set out in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which support subscription/redemption and HWM/performance-fee concepts generally. The framing reflects general industry practice for Category III equalisation accounting.
